title: You can’t silence us: A united front against Pomona’s repression

title: We will not tolerate collective punishment: Suspended students speak out

title: A guide to ballot propositions

title: Existential dread is an essential aspect of the liberal arts experience
first_p: embrace existential confusion about your future as part and parcel of the liberal arts college experience, writes yifei cheng po ’24.

title: Patriarchy doesn’t stop at the dinner table
first_p: mothers are often held to a much higher standard of judgment by their children, and you should learn to recognize that dynamic if it manifests in your family, writes shay suresh cm ’24.

title: Female athletes are more than just a uniform
first_p: we must put an end to the toxic culture of objectifying and sexualizing female athletes, writes annika reff po ‘25.

title: EDITORIAL BOARD: Two years in, what does it mean to come back together?
first_p: two years after the 5cs sent students home due to the covid-19 pandemic, the editorial board asks what it means to truly come together and build a more resilient community.

title: We must keep the classics alive
first_p: even as more students gravitate away from the humanities and toward stem fields, it is essential that liberal arts colleges recognize the continued value of the classics, writes annika reff po ’25.

title: Online school can work, if done right
first_p: online class,  as a supplement to in-person learning, has more potential to enrich students’ education than we may realize, writes alexander chao po ’25.

title: “Sad girl music,” and why fan culture is bad for art
first_p: the recent treatment of singer-songwriter mitski by her fans has illuminated how the way we consume art in the digital age could be harmful to both artist and the audience, argues nikki smith sc ‘25.

title: Queer representation doesn’t always look the way you expect
first_p: it’s time we recognize the potential for queer-coded characters to be meaningful to the queer community while recognizing the harmful motives behind “queerbaiting”, writes eliza powers po ‘25.

title: DIVERSITY & INCLUSION: Continuing our efforts to transform TSL’s newsroom
first_p: tsl aims to represent a diversity of communities within our staff and our coverage. but doing that effectively begins with an understanding of who’s been comfortable in our newsroom now and in the past — and who hasn’t felt as welcome. our presence in the predominantly white space of the

title: I am of Ukrainian heritage, and I’m proud of it
first_p: 5c students should understand the history of ukraine and stand in solidarity with the ukrainian people as they resist russian invasion, writes guest columnist valerie braylovskiy po ’25.

title: Distance doesn’t automatically mean breakup
first_p: a long distance relationship can lead to multiple benefits for a couple, despite the common stereotype that it will most likely result in breakup, writes anna tolkien cm ‘24.

title: The Claremont Colleges — and 5C students — must support the fight for affordable housing in Claremont
first_p: the claremont colleges need to own up to their role in perpetuating housing unaffordability in claremont, writes gwen tucker sc ’25.

title: Talk with the intention to listen
first_p: if you want to have meaningful and mutually satisfying conversations with people, start by actively listening to what they are saying, writes shay suresh cm ’24.

title: 5C students should not be subject to regressive ideas of modesty
first_p: the censorship of a portrait that the author sent for an instagram takeover for the pomona office of communications shows that even the 5cs are not immune to oppressive policing of female students’ attire, writes guest columnist eshanya agrawal po ’25.

title: It’s okay to talk about body-focused repetitive behaviors
first_p: we should not feel stigma around discussing body-focused repetitive behaviors, writes guest columnist maddy mccue cm ’23.

title: Forcing unvaccinated students to Oasis endangers public health
first_p: the pomona college administration is ignoring basic public health guidance by forcing students with medical exemptions to covid-19 vaccination to move to the oasis apartments and bundling them together in shared spaces, writes guest columnist gabe schuhl po ‘25.

title: Backlash against ‘race swapping’ in ‘The Rings of Power’ misses the point
first_p: opinion: a backlash against ‘race swapping’ in “the rings of power” reflects a dangerous misinterpretation of tolkien that gatekeeps the fantasy classic within a racialized framework, argues yifei cheng po ‘24.

title: Why self-help books can’t compete with interpersonal connections
first_p: opinion: self-help books, despite being designed to help people solve their personal problems without relying on others, cannot help as much as they promise, writes alexander chao po ’25.

title: Students are going hungry. Mutual aid can help
first_p: pitzer community fridge, a mutual aid initiative aiming to provide free and accessible food, can help address the issue of food insecurity facing 5c students, write guest columnists juliane hyvert sc ’25 and sydney watson sc ‘25.

title: We need to dismantle the beauty standard
first_p: comments putting down your friend’s appearance can still be hurtful even if they aren’t very overt, writes anna tolkien cm ’24.

title: ‘The women’s college’ isn’t just for women anymore
first_p: scripps must institute a truly coherent and inclusive policy on admission of transgender and non-binary applicants, as part of an ongoing re-evaluation of what it really means to be a “women’s college,” argues nicole smith sc ’25.

title: Find the Olympics a permanent home
first_p: the olympics should be moved to a permanent location, to mitigate the concerns about corruption, human rights, and environmental sustainability that have marred the 2022 winter olympics and previous games, argues annika reff po ’25.

title: Florida’s “Don’t Say Gay” bill represents a national attack on LGBTQIA+ acceptance in schools
first_p: florida’s “don’t say gay” bill follows a dangerous national trend of proposed and implemented legislation attacking the existence of lgbtqia+ students and families, says gwen tucker sc ‘25.

title: We owe Taylor Swift an apology
first_p: the media and public representation of taylor swift reminds us that we must confront our internalized misogyny and be more thoughtful with ourselves and other women, says shay suresh cm ‘24.

title: International students need more support as COVID-19 travel restrictions continue
first_p: the 5cs must offer more support to international students facing restrictions on travel to their home countries due to covid-19, with possible actions including recruitment of domestic host families over winter break and increased support with job and internship searches, writes scarlett liu cm ’24.

title: Nazi associations of Scripps statue call into question college’s commitments to inclusivity
first_p: the nazi ties of georg kolbe, 20th century german sculptor whose statue “young woman” is on display at scripps’ tiernan field house, require the college to re-evaluate the prominent position afforded to the statue in light of its stated commitment to inclusivity and tolerance, argues guest columnist lily dunkin sc ’24.

title: The 5Cs should make their courses hybrid-flexible this semester
first_p: the 5cs should offer a hybrid option so that immunocompromised students can choose to continue attending classes online, out of concern for their health amid a pandemic that is still not over, writes guest columnist luciénne reyes pz ’24.

title: Gamification can be a solution to improved health
first_p: gamification can be instrumental in transforming our relationship with health and motivating us to engage in healthy behaviors, writes alexander chao po ‘25.

title: Need-blind admission for international students is a necessity
first_p: pomona must extend its need-blind admissions policy to international students to fulfill its pledged commitment to affordable education, writes yifei cheng po ‘24.

title: Pomona must clarify its COVID-19 testing policy as students return to in-person learning
first_p: pomona college and student health services must reassess their covid-19 testing guidelines to accommodate false-positive cases and improve their lines of communication to address discrepancies in instructions given to students, writes annika reff po ’25.

title: EDITORIAL BOARD: Our staff are our backbone
first_p: we must not neglect gratitude to the 7c grounds staff and other campus workers who have invested tremendous time and effort into ensuring students’ safe and smooth return to campus during this unprecedented time, writes the tsl editorial board.

title: U.S. Holocaust education needs to be better, and so do 5C students
first_p: the recent banning of “maus” by a tennessee county school board is just one example of how education on the holocaust and modern-day anti-semitism is sorely lacking in the us, write nicole smith sc ’25 and gwen tucker sc ’25.

title: The gym isn’t a place for competition. Don’t make it one
first_p: 5c students must be welcoming to people of all fitness levels and maintain a positive dialogue surrounding exercise culture, instead of comparing and shaming others for their workout habits, writes anna tolkien cm ’24.

title: When it comes to self-care vs. academics, you can have both
first_p: amid a stressful return to campus, students should not feel guilty about making time for themselves and understand that academics and self-care do not need to be in conflict, writes shay suresh cm ’24.

title: After a pandemic semester, we shouldn’t have the added stress of finals
first_p: the stresses of in-person learning during a pandemic warrant making finals optional for this semester, if not canceling them, argue guest columnists rob zintl po ’23 and julia haudenschield sc ’23.

title: Mudders, 5C clubs want you
first_p: mudders shouldn’t be afraid to join 5c clubs, so that they can fully reap the benefits of the consortium, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: The 5Cs must take an active role in water conservation
first_p: california’s ongoing drought demands more active measures to conserve water from 5c colleges and their students, argues willa frank po ’25.

title: The 7Cs should incorporate sustainability throughout their curricula
first_p: the 7cs should implement a petition from claremont climate initiative to incorporate discussions of sustainability into their classes as much as possible, argues luciénne reyes pz ’24.

title: Registering for classes shouldn’t be so hard
first_p: the 5cs have a responsibility to fix the technical and accessibility issues that students experienced during recent course registration, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: The not-so-glamorous truth of being an international student at CMC
first_p: cmc needs to stop neglecting and dismissing international students’ needs, and work towards addressing them, argues guest columnist bertha tobias cm ’24.

title: Sibling rivalry should not define your life
first_p: don’t compete with your siblings, instead learn to be proud of their achievements and to define your own success, argues mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: DIVERSITY & INCLUSION EDITORS: Our progress on newsroom diversity & inclusion
first_p: as the student life works to serve the 7c community with integrity, the process of fostering accessibility needs to start within our own newsroom. that’s why we’re serving as tsl’s first-ever diversity & inclusion editors.

title: The issues with excluding allies and straight-passing queer people from queggers
first_p: advertising and policing ‘queggers’ as queer-only parties excludes straight identifying, questioning and closeted students, which can complicate lgbtq+ students’ experiences at them, argues porter reyes po ’25.

title: ‘Did I peak in high school?’ Let’s talk about impostor syndrome
first_p: addressing impostor syndrome with positive affirmations and reassuring conversations can avoid serious mental health consequences, argues shay suresh cm ’24.

title: Don’t lose yourself by saying ‘yes’
first_p: set limits to your ‘niceness’ so you don’t diminish your individuality or overextend yourself at the cost of your own well being, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: Don’t knock ASMR until you’ve tried it
first_p: everyone should look beyond their pre-conceived notions and give asmr a try, writes mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: Pomona College must divest from fossil fuels, but that’s not enough
first_p: pomona college must not only divest its endowment from fossil fuels, but ethically reinvest it through a transparent process that listens to student input, argues nicholas black po ’24.

title: APIDA face unique mental health issues
first_p: we need more support and research targeted toward apida communities, who suffer from greater mental health stigma and bicultural stress, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: The fragility of Roe v. Wade shows need for new abortion rights legislation
first_p: with ever greater efforts by red states to restrict or outright ban abortion, pro-choice activists should refocus their efforts away from preserving roe v. wade and more on enshrining new protections into law, argues abby loiselle po ’23.

title: Eliminate the zero-sum game of quota grading
first_p: quota grading fosters competition over collaboration and does not reward improvement, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: DIII women’s sports deserve greater institutional support
first_p: colleges have a responsibility to provide institutional support to division iii women’s athletes to help them make up for disparities in donations and networking opportunities, argues madison lewis po ’23.

title: You don’t truly know your home until you’ve gotten lost in it
first_p: allowing yourself to get lost in an unfamiliar place is a truly enlightening experience that everyone should have at least once, writes willa frank po ’25.

title: Cats aren’t just cute, they’re beneficial for your health
first_p: owning a cat has often underappreciated benefits for your mental health, writes mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: Support for Black students at Pitzer is long overdue
first_p: similarities between the 1968 and 2020 pitzer college black student union’s addresses are testament to the lack of development in support for black students, argues luciénne reyes pz ’24.

title: Fighting for the climate means upholding Indigenous sovereignty
first_p: fighting climate change requires renewed focus on protecting indigenous peoples’ sovereignty, and a reckoning with how our colleges and other institutions may be invested in fossil fuel projects that threaten indigenous land rights, argues guest columnist ethan vitaz pz ’22.

title: Don’t be fooled, your ‘baggage’ isn’t a burden
first_p: we should break the stigma around ‘oversharing’ and feel encouraged to share our real feelings with those we trust, argues shay suresh cm ’24.

title: California’s juvenile justice system needs a complete overhaul
first_p: a proposal to raise the minimum age at which california juveniles can be tried as adults is only scratching the surface of the complete transformation the state’s juvenile justice system badly needs, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: Mutual aid is the future of environmentalism
first_p: lack of action on the national level requires local communities to step up mutual aid efforts to protect the most vulnerable from the effects of climate change, argues nicholas black po ’24.

title: Mudders, take charge of your honor code
first_p: the harvey mudd honor code is under threat, and infractions may have a bigger impact than we realize, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: Missing people you’ve never met is a valid experience
first_p: grieving for someone you have never met is a valid and normal experience, argues mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: Yik Yak is the unspoken hero of the 5Cs
first_p: anonymous messaging app yik yak provides a crucial outlet for students to be honest about their problems and find support from their peers, writes porter reyes po ’25.

title: California can’t afford more spills — stop current and future offshore oil drilling
first_p: the orange county oil spill provides further evidence that california must end all offshore oil drilling in the state, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: 5C students should reexamine their regional biases
first_p: some 5c students’ stereotyping of central and southern areas of the us as backward and intolerant is unfair and can blind us to persistent inequities where we live, argues madison lewis po ’23.

title: Highway 101 wildlife corridor could make LA County a beacon of conservation
first_p: with construction set to begin next year on a wildlife corridor across highway 101, which will be the world’s largest, los angeles county marks a new standard for habitat conservation in the united states, writes willa frank po ’25.

title: Pomona College has failed in its handling of COVID-19
first_p: pomona college’s handling of covid-19 cases on campus has been worrying, inefficient and endangering, argues abby loiselle po ’23.

title: Find the line between humorous self-deprecation and self-hatred
first_p: limit your self deprecating humor to avoid affecting your self-esteem and self-perception, argues mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: We need more women-specific academic programs at the 5Cs
first_p: the claremont colleges must devote more resources to female students’ academic development and to programs that confront systemic challenges in academia, argues yutong niu po ’23.

title: Harvey Mudd first-years need sleep, not 8 a.m. classes
first_p: pushing back the start times of hmc core classes means students will be better rested and more productive, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: The global supply chain is breaking down
first_p: the breakdown of global supply chains requires us to reevaluate our consumption choices, argues willa frank po ’25.

title: Hate incident demonstrates problems of Pitzer’s culture of ‘white allyship’
first_p: the reactions to a hateful comment recently reported at pitzer are a reminder that conversations about prejudice must start from a place of support for and centering of marginalized individuals’ voices, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: 5C students deserve better mental health resources
first_p: the 5cs must dedicate more resources to providing accessible and in-person mental health support for students, especially with the added stresses of a return to on-campus learning, argues nicholas black po ’24.

title: ‘Hamilton’ discrimination allegations raise questions about the real meaning of inclusivity
first_p: recent allegations of severe discrimination against minorities on the set of the broadway musical ‘hamilton’ demonstrate that simply hiring a diverse group of people is not enough for a truly inclusive environment, argues guest columnist caelan reeves cm ’24.

title: Appreciate, don’t appropriate other cultures
first_p: someone’s culture is not your accessory or prop; understand the context and significance to appreciate and not appropriate, argues shay suresh cm ’24.

title: First-years at Harvey Mudd, there’s no rush to date
first_p: harvey mudd freshies should take their time to start dating, and first prioritize adjusting to college life and academics, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: Don’t buy into the false allure of dieting products
first_p: avoid diet plans and products that promote unhealthy habits, and instead prioritize your health, argues mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: It’s time to rethink cross-campus dining
first_p: cross-campus dining can be reopened while keeping covid-19 spread under control, argues madison lewis po ’24.

title: Save lives by keeping AB 988 alive
first_p: assembly bill 988 will save lives by providing funding for california’s mental health crisis response system, but we need to advocate for it now so it will pass, argues porter reyes po ’25.

title: Blame corporations rather than entry-level workers for unethical practices
first_p: many students and other entry-level workers don’t have the luxury of choosing a job that precisely aligns with their ethical principles, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: CMC trustees must divest from the Coastal GasLink pipeline
first_p: cmc trustees henry kravis and george roberts should end their connections to the cgl pipeline, which contributes to climate change and violates the sovereignty of the wet’suwet’en people, luciénne reyes pz ’24 writes.

title: You don’t need to buy a new iPhone every year
first_p: resist the social pressure to buy a new iphone every year as it feeds into wasteful and consumerist behaviors, argues mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: Harvey Mudd should solicit student input on COVID-19 policies
first_p: harvey mudd college needs to solicit more student opinion in the covid-19 policy making process, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: It’s okay to not be happy back on campus
first_p: a return to campus has brought new challenges coupled with romanticized expectations, says abby loiselle po ’23.

title: Politicians shouldn’t be your idols
first_p: stop idolizing politicians, and hold them accountable for their actions, argues nicholas black po ’24.

title: When it comes to academic teamwork, collaborate with caution
first_p: while harvey mudd college’s approach of collaboration for school work has its benefits, beware of the often overlooked downsides, argues serena mao hm ’25.

title: Pausing Spectrum 10K isn’t enough to support the autistic community
first_p: the spectrum 10k study into biological influences on autism promotes harmful and disproven stigmas about autistic people and should be stopped altogether, argues luciénne reyes pz ’24.

title: Faith is a choice, not an inheritance
first_p: the religion a person practices upon growing up should be their choice alone, writes shay suresh cm ’24.

title: Make an effort to pronounce people’s names correctly
first_p: making a genuine effort to pronounce a person’s name correctly is a crucial sign of respect for their unique identity, writes mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: Financial literacy can’t fix socioeconomic inequality
first_p: the emphasis on financial education as a strategy to reduce economic inequality is a false solution that blames poor people for situations often beyond their control, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: Boredom is an essential form of self-care
first_p: learning to appreciate boredom can improve our mental health and creativity, writes mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: Pomona should pull its weight in municipal organic recycling
first_p: pomona college should take charge of its own food waste management instead of depending on the city of claremont’s overburdened compost system, argues willa frank po ’25.

title: We should get more bang for our (flex) bucks
first_p: pomona college should expand students’ ability to use flex bucks for essentials other than food, argues porter reyes po ’25.

title: It takes more than word policing to fight prejudice
first_p: preventing others from using words that most people don’t find offensive is not an effective way to fight discrimination, writes kenny le pz ’25.

title: The 5Cs must prioritize athletes’ mental health
first_p: the 5cs must regard mental health among athletes as equally important as physical health, argues abby loiselle po ’23.

title: California recall election shows that voting in college doesn’t have to be a hassle
first_p: the california gubernatorial recall election demonstrates why vote by mail should be made more accessible and widespread, especially for students, argues madison lewis po ’23.

title: The 5Cs are responsible for promoting safe alcohol use on campus
first_p: role models that students are exposed to upon entering college are crucial for the development of a culture of responsible drinking on campus, writes serena mao hm ’25.

title: Don’t scapegoat social media alone for poor mental health
first_p: the alleged harm that social media poses to mental health is largely exaggerated, and we should learn how to use social media responsibly rather than reject it, argues kenny le pz ’25.

title: The humanities are just as important as STEM
first_p: the upheaval of the covid-19 pandemic demonstrates that the humanities are just as important as stem fields in building a healthy society, writes mishaal ijaz sc ’24.

title: Biden must keep his healthcare promise
first_p: voters must hold president biden to his campaign promise to pass a public option, so that america can finally achieve the goal of universal health coverage, writes nicholas black po ’24.

title: Flipped classrooms should have no place at the 5Cs
first_p: flipped classrooms are a fad, hurting students more than they help, says serena mao hm ’25.

title: Pomona must address stresses faced by international students during distance learning
first_p: pomona college must acknowledge the treatment of international students during the covid-19 pandemic and increase institutional support for them, writes yutong niu po ’23.

title: Socializing can wait, your mental health can’t
first_p: avoid social burnout from returning to campus by prioritizing your mental health, says shay suresh cm ’24.
